transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sophie Lin (Redwood Product), Lisa Grant (Renaissance Head of Data), Ahmed Khan (Renaissance Lead ML), Priya Rao (Renaissance Infosec), Tom Weller (Cloud Architect)

Summary:
Quick onramp demo focused on switching inference endpoints from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Covered parity mapping, console walkthrough (routes, rollouts, cost/latency dashboards), Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quant profiles), and pilot plan. Customer had strong security questions (VPC/KMS, audit logs).

Topics:
- Migration strategy and equivalence mapping
- Console: routes, rollouts, model catalog
- Redwood Optimize: batching, KV cache, quantization advice
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs
- Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2, access control
- Pilot next steps and benchmarks

Action items (recap in call): see metadata

Transcript body:
[00:00:01] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side — I'm Maya, AE. Diego and Sophie from product/team with me.
[00:00:12] Lisa: Hi Maya. Hi Diego. thanks. Lisa here — we'll just jump in.
[00:00:20] Diego: Hi all. I'm Diego, I'm the SE who will be running the bench and the console walkthrough.
[00:00:28] Ahmed: Ahmed here. we'll be evaluating perf and cost against our current OpenAI endpoints.
[00:00:32] Maya: Great. high level agenda: 1) parity mapping between your existing endpoints and Redwood API, 2) console tour, 3) Optimize suggestions, 4) next steps and pilot.
[00:00:44] Tom: quick note — our infra folks care about private deployment options, VPC peering, KMS. Priya will lead security questions.
[00:00:52] Priya: yep. encryption at rest, HSM/KMS integration, audit logs — we'd like to see retention policies.
[00:01:00] Diego: makes sense. we'll show the private deployment checklist and where the audit logs surface in the console.
[00:01:08] Maya: ok starting parity mapping. so most customers we see are on OpenAI/Anthropic/Together. the mapping strategy is twofold: API equivalence (same prompt/response shapes, tool-calling mappings) and runtime tuning (batching, kv cache for chat workloads).
[00:01:25] Lisa: how much changes in the prompt layer? like do we need new system instructions?
[00:01:30] Diego: usually minimal. you can keep system prompts, we support function-calls and structured output. some token-cost differences appear based on model choice and tokenization differences — we can normalize via small prompt wrappers.
[00:01:44] Ahmed: tokenization differences — can you give an example? we had weird token delta when moving from Anthropic to Together earlier.
[00:01:50] Diego: yeah a common example is names and special chars — depending on tokenizer you might see +/− 5-15% tokens. We recommend profiling using sample traffic; that's why we'll ask for 100 sample prompts to measure distribution.
[00:02:04] [00:02:05] Sophie: also important is sequence length distribution — Optimize uses that to recommend batching and kv cache SLOs.
[00:02:12] Lisa: walk us through the console.
[00:02:15] Diego: switching screens now — demoing Redwood Console. top is model catalog, you can pin model versions per route. here you define routes that map to your service endpoints, then assign rollout policies — canary, A/B, fallback chains.
[00:02:33] [00:02:35] Maya: show the cost vs latency panel — it's token-level and route-level, so you can see per-route spend.
[00:02:40] Diego: here's our Optimize recommendations tab — it highlights opportunities like enabling prefix cache for chat sessions, suggested batch size for GPUs, and a quantization profile suggestion based on model variant and perf target.
[00:02:52] Ahmed: what's the default batch sizing? we're very latency sensitive for our triage chat use case (p95 < 400ms).
[00:02:58] Diego: default is small — continuous batching with dynamic time windows. for strict p95 SLOs we recommend dedicated pools with latency-optimized kernels and smaller effective batch sizes; Optimize can simulate p95 impact. we also do GPU kernel switching for short sequences to keep tail latency low.
[00:03:13] Maya: and on the hosted plan we expose routing by policy so you can route low-latency requests to higher-tier pools and cheap background requests to more cost-efficient variants.
[00:03:22] Priya: can you explain data retention on hosted? we need logs for auditing but cannot retain payloads beyond X days.
[00:03:29] Sophie: we have configurable retention per-account — also for enterprise we can disable payloads in logs and only keep metadata. Private deployment gives you full control over retention.
[00:03:40] Tom: VPC peering — does Redwood manage the control plane in your VPC or ours?
[00:03:45] Diego: for Private we run a customer-managed control plane — you either run our on-prem package or we set up a VPC with private control plane and you handle peering. encryption keys can be in your KMS/HSM.
[00:03:56] [00:03:58] Ahmed: performance bench details — what will Diego run?
[00:04:02] Diego: I'll run a small script that replays your 100 prompts with original concurrency and measure throughput/latency and cost per token. we'll also run a KV cache scenario for chat to show delta on token usage.
[00:04:14] Lisa: cool. about quantization — our models are Llama variants. how safe is the quality after int8 quantization?
[00:04:20] Diego: we do model-specific quant profiles: for many Llama variants, int8 or mixed int8-16 is acceptable with minimal degradation for generation tasks. Optimize will surface WER/approximate similarity metrics against a holdout eval set. we also recommend canary rollouts to validate quality.
[00:04:36] [00:04:38] Maya: important tradeoff callout: more aggressive quantization reduces cost but can increase hallucination risk on certain instruction-following prompts. we detect regressions via eval hooks.
[00:04:49] Priya: on eval hooks — are prompts and responses stored for quality monitoring? we need to ensure PHI isn't logged.
[00:04:55] Sophie: you can exclude PHI at ingestion or mask at routing. for pilot, best practice is to hash or scrub sensitive fields and run quality hooks on masked data.
[00:05:05] Ahmed: can we keep a versioned prompt set to compare outputs?
[00:05:09] Diego: yes; console has eval sets and you can tie them to rollouts so a canary is only promoted if eval metrics pass.
[00:05:16] Lisa: let's talk cost parity — we currently pay X with OpenAI; how do you model that?
[00:05:21] Maya: we'll build a tailored cost model based on your token distribution and sequence length profile. Optimize suggests batching/caching steps that usually reduce unit cost 20–50% depending on workload. Diego will run the replay to give a concrete comparison.
[00:05:35] Ahmed: does Redwood bill per token the same way? any hidden egress/net fees?
[00:05:40] Maya: hosted has per-token pricing and embedding pricing. egress within region is standard — we disclose all fees. Dedicated is usually a committed monthly capacity model which helps predictably control unit economics.
[00:05:52] Tom: curious about fallbacks — say Redwood model variant is unavailable, can we fallback to OpenAI?
[00:05:57] Diego: yes you can configure multi-provider fallbacks in routing policies; many customers use Redwood as primary and a public provider as fallback during autoscaling spikes.
[00:06:06] [00:06:08] Lisa: let's walk the pilot plan. what are tangible success criteria?
[00:06:12] Maya: suggested pilot: 2 weeks. goals: parity in output quality for 90% of eval prompts, p95 latency within 1.2x of current, and a cost target (e.g., <0.9x current or agreed threshold).
[00:06:25] Ahmed: acceptable. we'll provide eval set + sample traffic.
[00:06:29] Priya: security gating — we need SOC2, ISOs, and a contract clause on data handling.
[00:06:34] Maya: we'll share SOC2 docs and the private deployment checklist. for contract clauses we can loop Legal.
[00:06:40] [00:06:42] Diego: quick demo of a KV cache scenario: here's a chat session — with prefix cache enabled we rehydrate KV and reduce repeated context tokens by 40%. watching console metrics, token spend is cut and latency remains stable.
[00:06:56] Ahmed: interesting. do you expose cache hit rate metrics?
[00:06:59] Diego: yep, per-route cache hit/miss rates, and you can visualize them over time; Optimize will estimate savings if you enable cache for certain routes.
[00:07:08] Lisa: any gotchas when porting function calling from OpenAI?
[00:07:12] Diego: function calling semantics are supported; you might need to map field names if you relied on specific provider quirks. we recommend a small adapter shim during pilot.
[00:07:21] [00:07:24] Maya: circling back on private vs hosted — for a regulated health customer with PHI, Private with VPC + customer-managed keys is common. Hosted can still work if you can mask PHI pre-ingest.
[00:07:35] Tom: how long to spin up dedicated pools?
[00:07:38] Sophie: dedicated pool lead time depends on quota and hardware — typically 2-6 weeks for reserved capacity; pilot can run on hosted or smaller dedicated test pools.
[00:07:48] Ahmed: any latency guarantees? we need to know realistic p95.
[00:07:52] Diego: we publish historical SLOs for model categories. for hard p95 SLOs customers go Dedicated and we tune batch windows and kernels. we'll share sample traces from similar customers.
[00:07:59] [00:08:02] Priya: on compliance, do you support SAML/SSO and SCIM?
[00:08:06] Maya: yes, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, audit logs — all standard on enterprise.
[00:08:13] Lisa: could you show us where to set rollout policies?
[00:08:16] Diego: click into a route -> rollouts -> new policy. you can select canary percentage, time window, auto rollback on eval regressions. also add fallback chain.
[00:08:29] [00:08:31] Diego: demoing canary: creating canary at 5% for 30 minutes. tie eval gates — if QPS or similarity drops go below threshold, it auto-rolls back.
[00:08:41] Ahmed: sweet. about telemetry — do we get token-level breakdown per API key?
[00:08:45] Sophie: yes per-token breakdown exposed through console and the billing API, so you can attribute costs to services.
[00:08:52] Lisa: this is helpful. the one remaining piece is the costs of the pilot — will this be free?
[00:08:57] Maya: pilot pricing is flexible — we typically offer a small credit for evaluation; detailed SOW will outline the terms.
[00:09:05] [00:09:08] Tom: any gotchas with region placement? our data residency is EU-only for some flows.
[00:09:13] Diego: we support region pinning and private deployments in EU. for hosted EU we have region availability; we'll confirm specific regions in the follow-up.
[00:09:22] Priya: key rotation and audit — can we bring our own key?
[00:09:26] Sophie: yes, BYOK via KMS integration for Private; for hosted you can use our key management or integrate external KMS for encryption at rest in some configs.
[00:09:36] Ahmed: ok next steps: we'll collect sample prompts and constraints; you will send SOW/pricing and security docs.
[00:09:42] Maya: correct — action items as discussed.
[00:09:46] [00:09:50] Lisa: quick question — do you support streaming responses? we rely on chunked streaming for UX.
[00:09:54] Diego: yes streaming with chunked responses and token-level progress events; also function-call stream mode.
[00:09:59] Maya: any other questions?
[00:10:02] Priya: I might have an offline question about encryption key escrow. will email.
[00:10:06] Tom: I'll coordinate getting infra signup info for peering.
[00:10:09] Ahmed: we'll target sending prompts and eval by Friday.
[00:10:12] Maya: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with SOW and cost model.
[00:10:16] [00:32:59] (note: the recording shows some silences and screen-share only segments where Diego ran a live perf script and showed console graphs, timestamps omitted)
[00:33:10] Diego: results summary from the replay: median latency comparable to current, p95 within 1.1x for the short-seq chat route when using dedicated pool config. token spend per session dropped ~28% with KV caching enabled.
[00:33:24] Ahmed: that's promising. what's the % variability run-to-run?
[00:33:28] Diego: we saw 5-8% variance for short bursts, larger variability under sustained concurrency spikes — that's where routing policy + fallback helps.
[00:33:36] [00:33:40] Lisa: Sophie can you attach the sample console screenshots to the follow-up email?
[00:33:44] Sophie: yes will attach.
[00:33:48] Priya: please include the private deployment checklist and the data handling section.
[00:33:52] Maya: will do.
[00:33:56] [00:34:00] Diego: final note — sometimes transcriptions show KV as 'k v cash' in older logs, so ignore weird transcribe tokens.
[00:34:07] Ahmed: haha noted.
[00:34:10] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll send the follow-ups.
[00:34:14] Lisa: thanks all.
[00:34:16] (call end)
